newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN CLABECQ WORKERS CALL FOR MORE TALKS - RADIO.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN CLABECQ WORKERS CALL FOR MORE TALKS - RADIO.

text.p: Workers at bankrupt steel maker Forges de Clabecq SA , meeting at a general assembly on Friday, have called for more discussions on Clabecq's future, Belgian radio said on Friday.
Receivers appointed to keep Clabecq running have proposed immediately re-employing about 1,400 of the firm's 1,800 employees whom they are laying off.
Clabecq personnel wanted to return to work but were concerned about other employees who were to be pensioned off and also wanted more security in their new contracts, the radio said.
"We want to work. We're not on strike - the company has stopped us working," one employee told RTBF radio.

They called on Clabecq management, the Walloon region and the president of the court which declared Clabecq bankrupt on January 3 to hold "serious" talks, and they arranged another general assembly of workers for January 18.

The Walloon region, Clabecq's majority shareholder, said on Thursday the receivers' proposals were necessary for activity to continue at the firm, and reiterated that Clabecq's long term survival depended on a total or partial takeover by an industrial operator.

Clabecq filed for bankruptcy in mid-December after the European Commission rejected a 1.5 billion Belgian franc ($47 million) rescue plan by the Walloon Region, which then withdrew its support from the firm.
The company's shares were this week delisted from the Brussels bourse this week where they had been quoted on the cash market.
